usage: This is the most common and versatile way to say goodbye in Cairo, suitable for both formal and casual situations. It is used by people of all ages and social classes when parting ways. You can say this to a single person or a group without needing to change the phrasing.

variants.label: casual
variants.note: Borrowed from English, this is extremely common among friends, family, and younger people.

variants.label: see you later (to a man)
variants.note: Used casually when you expect to see the person again soon.

variants.label: see you later (to a woman)
variants.note: The feminine equivalent for saying see you later.

variants.label: good night (to a man)
variants.note: Used specifically when parting ways late at night or before going to sleep.

responses.english: may God keep you safe (to a man)
may God keep you safe (to a woman)

examples.arabic: أَنَا لَازِم أَمْشِي دِلْوَقْتِي، مَعَ السَّلَامَة.
examples.transliteration: ana lazem amshi delwa2ti, ma3a el salama.
examples.english: I have to go now, goodbye.

examples.arabic: مَعَ السَّلَامَة يَا جَمَاعَة، خَلُّوا بَالْكُم مِن نَفْسُكُم.
examples.transliteration: ma3a el salama ya gama3a, khallou balkom men nafsokom.
examples.english: Goodbye guys, take care of yourselves.
